result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Baseline eShopLegacyNTier handwritten source and configuration reviewed for embedded passwords/keys, credential use, permission assignment and audit logging. LocalDB connection string has no embedded credential; public key tokens and service addresses are not secrets. Missing application authentication is not automatically classified as CWE-732 without a concrete incorrect permission assignment. No actual secret values included. Host ACLs, IIS authentication overrides, environment values and external auditing unavailable to static assessment.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.UpdateCatalogItem marks the submitted entity Modified and calls SaveChanges at lines 75-76 without an application audit record of actor, item identity, old/new values or outcome. The remotely exposed operation can alter catalog prices and image filenames. A service-reachable actor can change an item and later restore its values without an application-level trace of the intermediate change. No audit interceptor or logging sink is wired in the assessed source/configuration. IIS access logs or externally configured SQL/database auditing may exist outside this repository; their absence is not asserted. The finding concerns missing semantic application audit events, not a demonstrated bypass of external monitoring.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
